It's important to note that this courthouse is listed on the National Register of Historic Places, possibly from 1973, and contributes to the local historic district.**Compiling Museum and Courthouse Info**

The 1881 Courthouse Museum is operated by the Custer County Historical Society, open from May to September, featuring exhibits on local history such as the gold rush and Native American culture. Here’s a concise overview of the Custer County Courthouse in South Dakota and what people generally mean when they refer to it:

What it is
- The historic county courthouse in the city of Custer (the county seat of Custer County, South Dakota). 
- Commonly known today as the 1881 Courthouse Museum, because the former courthouse now operates as a local history museum.

Location
- Custer, South Dakota (in the Black Hills). The historic building sits along Mt. Rushmore Road in downtown Custer.

History and use
- Constructed in 1880–1881 to serve as Custer County’s courthouse during the Black Hills’ early settlement/gold‑rush period.
- Functioned as the county’s primary courthouse for many decades (into the 20th century), after which county governmental and judicial functions moved to a modern courthouse building elsewhere in Custer.
- The original courthouse was preserved and converted to the 1881 Courthouse Museum, which interprets regional history.

Architecture and significance
- A two‑story, wood‑frame, clapboard building with a prominent central cupola/tower—typical of late‑19th‑century frontier civic architecture in the region.
- Noted as one of the earliest surviving public buildings in the Black Hills and an emblem of the establishment of formal county government following the Black Hills gold discoveries of the 1870s.
- Listed on the National Register of Historic Places (NRHP) under its historic courthouse name. Its NRHP status recognizes its importance in government and settlement history and its representative frontier‑era civic architecture.

Today (as the 1881 Courthouse Museum)
- Operated by the local historical organization as a museum.
- Exhibits generally cover:
  - The Black Hills gold rush and mining
  - Pioneer and ranching life
  - Development of Custer and Custer County government
  - Regional military and exploration history (including the Custer expedition context)
  - Native American (Lakota/Sioux) history and culture in the area
- Typically open seasonally (late spring through early fall); hours and programming vary year to year.

Notes and clarifications
- “Custer County Courthouse” can refer either to the historic 1881 building (now the museum) or to the current, modern courthouse where county government and the circuit court operate today. If you need records, hearings, or county services, you’ll want the current courthouse; if you’re visiting for history, you’ll want the 1881 Courthouse Museum.
- Don’t confuse it with the Custer County Courthouse in Nebraska (also historic and NRHP‑listed) or with courthouses in other states named for Custer County.

If you’d like, I can pull current visiting hours, admission information, or the exact street addresses for both the museum (historic courthouse) and the present-day courthouse.
